authors: Andrew F. Hayes and Klaus Krippendorff
title: Answering the Call for a Standard Reliability Measure for Coding Data
use: Nominal alpha accommodates multiple independent coders. Report it as a descriptive consistency measure on comparable units; it does not validate substantive conclusions.

authors: John L. Campbell, Charles Quincy, Jordan Osserman, and Ove K. Pedersen
title: Coding In-depth Semistructured Interviews: Problems of Unitization and Intercoder Reliability and Agreement
use: Separate unit definition, independent reliability, and negotiated agreement. Their combined-code example moved from 54% independent agreement to 96% negotiated agreement, not to 96% independent reliability.

title: Intercoder Reliability in Qualitative Research: Debates and Practical Guidelines
use: No universal acceptance threshold. Consensus discussion is a legitimate reconciliation method. Reliability should fit the purpose and epistemic approach of the research, and does not establish validity.

authors: Klaus Krippendorff, interviewed by Jefferson Pooley; transcript substantially edited by Krippendorff
title: Communication Scholars Oral History Project: Klaus Krippendorff
use: Discusses approximately 0.800 and 0.667 alpha conventions and emphasizes consequences of incorrect conclusions. Used for contextual explanation only; no threshold was added to the frozen study.
